agentDebugRuns.summary: MVP delivery stayed steady: 2 of 3 delivery tasks were completed, including routing stabilization and the inbox acknowledgement patch.

highlights: MVP delivery stayed steady: 2 of 3 delivery tasks were completed, including routing stabilization and the inbox acknowledgement patch.
You completed 4 work sessions this week, and the completed blocks finished without interruptions.
Momentum returned after a disrupted prompt-review session, and the follow-up block successfully refined the reflection coach prompts.
blockers: Recovery work lagged behind delivery work: the recovery goal still shows 0 of 2 tasks completed.
Meeting-heavy windows interrupted planned focus time and contributed to lower focus and higher stress mid-week.
Short sleep mid-week (330 minutes) dragged energy down, and fatigue stayed elevated late in the sprint.
The missed call window review remains blocked, leaving a small recovery/admin loop open.
trends: Focus and energy started strong, dipped when interruptions increased, and then partially recovered after tasks were reduced into smaller blocks.
Stress and fatigue signals were highest during meeting-heavy periods, while audio and video indicators improved after the recovery day.
Sleep improved from 330 to 405 minutes by the end of the week, which aligned with better recovery signals even though delivery remained the main focus.
nextSuggestions: Close the final delivery task with one clearly scoped 30-minute block so the MVP goal reaches 3 of 3.
Schedule a short recovery block early in the week to turn the sleep trend review into a completed task.
Use smaller restart steps after meetings to protect focus when your schedule gets fragmented.
Unblock the missed-call review with a quick 15-minute pass and decide immediately whether it needs follow-up or can be closed.
